props.gloss_en: the court ordinarily collects damages from property carrying a lien, i.e. land
if the injured party already seized movables, the court collects for him from them
Rabba bar Ulla's first definition: shaveh kesef means land, which is not subject to price-fraud law
Rabba bar Ulla's second definition: shaveh kesef means land, which is acquired with money
Rav Ashi: shaveh kesef means valuable but not money; portable valuables function like money, leaving land as the contrast
the verse yashiv includes payment in any equivalent value, even bran
when collecting inherited liability from orphans, only inherited liened land is available
the movables clause concerns seizure while the liable father was still alive

objections.gloss_en: the definition fails because slaves and documents also are not subject to price fraud
the replacement definition fails because slaves and documents also are acquired with money
one baraita restricts court collection to land; another validates even bran

answered_by.gloss_en: the land-only baraita concerns inherited liability collected from orphans

objections.gloss_en: if the case is orphans, why may seized movables be retained?

answered_by.gloss_en: the injured party seized them while the liable person was alive
